## Why this survey exists {#question}

Some people open AI to finish work quickly; others want a discussion partner. Some start with a page of context, others with “What do you think?” Some love the ideas; others cannot stand confident nonsense. How does the same technology become such different companions?

This is an informal MBTI × AI survey. We want real everyday habits, opinions and stories: what people use AI for, how they talk to it, what they enjoy and what annoys them. We will look for tendencies between reported types and variety within each type. There is no predetermined winning personality, and you do not need to prove your AI skills.

## An atlas we can build together {#outputs}

Once real responses arrive, we hope to build an atlas of how 16 personality types live with AI: habit charts, praise and complaint distributions, true stories quoted with permission, and an evolving observation article. We will state usable response counts and counts for each type; types without data stay blank. Small differences and many exceptions are interesting too. These are planned outputs; no participant statistics are currently reported.

## How the forms work {#design}

Think about the past 30 days. Quick choices contain 19 items and the story form 11, with 7 shared items. Totals include optional and conditional items; only applicable questions appear. One form is enough; use the same report ID to add the other. Uncertain MBTI skips the source question. Recent nonusers answer why they have not used AI, without inventing an experience. The final one-sentence reflection is optional. Choices describe uses, conversation habits and opinions; stories add context. Each item’s purpose can be opened, and that exposure is recorded. Actual completion time still needs human pilot feedback.

- **A little about you** (A01, A02, A03, A04) — An uncertain MBTI type is welcome. No need to take another test.
- **How AI fits your day** (Q01, Q02) — Think about everyday use over the past 30 days, not just your best experience.
- **How you like to chat** (Q03, Q04, Q05, Q06, Q07) — Choose what best matches your habits. There is no correct style.
- **Praise it. Complain about it.** (Q08, Q09, Q10, Q11, Q12) — You can like it, dislike it, or feel both ways.
- **Your AI story** (S01, S02, S03, S04) — Tell it like you would to a friend. A few sentences are fine.
- **One last thought** (A05, A06, A07) — Choose what may be shared, then review and export.

## What we will do with responses {#analysis}

First report valid counts and option percentages for each item, then explore distributions by MBTI, type source, frequency and experience. Multiple-choice percentages may exceed 100%. Missing, inapplicable, uncertain and explicit absence remain distinct. Satisfaction is a self-report, and checking frequency is not checking quality. Code stories for uses, conversation habits, benefits, complaints and exceptions, preserving opposing accounts; quote verbatim only with A05 permission. Do not double-count both forms, an Issue and its PR, or corrections from one person, or treat an independent study as one participant.

## What we cannot conclude {#limitations}

This volunteer internet sample describes contributors, not all people in the 16 types. It cannot establish personality causation or superior work ability. Small samples do not justify forced rankings or significance claims. The forms are not equivalent scales; the 12 translations have not undergone native-speaker cognitive interviews or cross-cultural measurement validation. Keep instrument language, switching history and the language of each answer; report languages and versions separately before considering any justified pooling. Keep old v0.2 single-task reports separate from v0.3 everyday-habit records.

## Understanding personality labels {#background}

MBTI is a conversation starter, not a personality assessment conducted here. Keep formal MBTI, 16Personalities, other tests, self-judgment and uncertainty distinct rather than treating them as one instrument. We do not copy commercial test items or use types to select people. Wording, format and order can affect responses, so pilot feedback on unclear wording and missing options will guide versioned revisions. [@mbti-ethics; @sixteen-framework; @pew-questions]

## Taking part and sharing {#availability}

Participation is voluntary for adults aged 18 or older who understand their chosen language, including recent nonusers. Complete the online form or download the standalone HTML for offline use, inspect and export JSON data and a Markdown report, then return them through an Issue or PR. The form does not upload answers automatically. Readable Markdown forms are also available; retain item IDs, confirmations, version and purpose-exposure records. GitHub submissions are public and linked to accounts; a report ID is not anonymity. Remove private, client, employer-confidential and credential information. Aggregate-use consent and quotation permission are separate; do not redistribute individual data freely without separate authorization. Request withdrawal at the original submission; later analyses exclude it, but downloaded or forked copies may remain. [@github-pages; @github-attachments]

## AI assistance and authorship {#ai-use}

Project byline: lawyer112. Codex assists with drafting, translation, implementation and checks; these are not native-speaker or independent researcher validation. Experiences must be the participant’s own; disclose AI writing help in A06. Exclude all TEST_ONLY fixtures. Real responses, independent studies, translation corrections and design ideas are welcome. Acknowledgement is voluntary, and paper authorship follows actual contributions.
